sentences.en: Back in 2018, my editor asked me to look into DNA Ancestry kits, which were becoming really popular.
sentences.zh: 早在2018年，我的编辑就让我去调查当时正变得非常热门的DNA祖源测试盒。

sentences.en: So much so that on Black Friday the year before, 23andMe's DNA test had actually been one of Amazon's top five bestsellers.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，在前一年的黑色星期五，23andMe的DNA测试实际上已经成为亚马逊最畅销的产品前五名之一。

sentences.en: The marketing for these tests was really clever and convincing.
sentences.zh: 这些测试的营销非常聪明且极具说服力。

sentences.en: When people got results that they expected, they'd say stuff like, I'm 68% Italian, so no wonder I like pasta.
sentences.zh: 当人们得到符合预期的结果时，他们会说诸如“我有68%的意大利血统，难怪我喜欢吃通心粉”这样的话。

sentences.en: But what about people who were stunned by their results?
sentences.zh: 但是那些被测试结果惊呆了的人呢？

sentences.en: I met one woman whose ancestry percentages totally challenged who she thought she was.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了一位女性，她的祖源百分比完全颠覆了她对自己的认知。

sentences.en: My name is Ruth Padower and I'm a contributor to the New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫露丝·帕多弗，我是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: I wrote a story about the rise of at-home DNA tests and how these kits claimed to tell us who we really are.
sentences.zh: 我写了一篇关于家用DNA测试兴起的故事，以及这些测试盒如何声称能告诉我们“我们究竟是谁”。

sentences.en: At the center of my story is Sigrid Johnson, who was raised by Black parents and went to a historically Black university.
sentences.zh: 我故事的核心人物是西格丽德·约翰逊，她由黑人父母抚养长大，并就读于一所历史悠久的黑人大学。

sentences.en: When Sigrid was 16, she found out that she was adopted.
sentences.zh: 西格丽德16岁时，发现自己是被收养的。

sentences.en: Her mom told her that Sigrid's biological mother was Italian and her bio father was Black.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲告诉她，西格丽德的亲生母亲是意大利人，亲生父亲是黑人。

sentences.en: When I met her, she was 65.
sentences.zh: 当我遇到她时，她65岁。

sentences.en: A few years earlier, she had taken a DNA test to find out her ancestry.
sentences.zh: 几年前，她做了一次DNA测试来查明自己的祖源。

sentences.en: The results said she was only 2.987% African.
sentences.zh: 结果显示她只有2.987%的非洲血统。

sentences.en: 2.987% is a really specific number and a really low percentage for a woman who had always thought she was Black.
sentences.zh: 对一个一直以为自己是黑人的女性来说，2.987%是一个非常具体的数字，也是一个极低的百分比。

sentences.en: After we met, Sigrid decided to try again.
sentences.zh: 我们见面后，西格丽德决定再试一次。

sentences.en: She took DNA tests from two more companies and suddenly she no longer tested as
sentences.zh: 她又购买了另外两家公司的DNA测试，突然之间，她的检测结果不再是

sentences.en: 2.987% African.
sentences.zh: 2.987%的非洲血统了。

sentences.en: One of the new tests concluded she was 27% African.
sentences.zh: 其中一项新测试得出结论，她有27%的非洲血统。

sentences.en: The other said she was 43.4%.
sentences.zh: 另一项则显示她有43.4%。

sentences.en: Of course, Sigrid's true ancestry, whatever it really is, had never changed.
sentences.zh: 当然，西格丽德真正的血统，无论它到底是什么，从未改变过。

sentences.en: I started to look into how reliable all these numbers were and how transparent the companies were about their methods.
sentences.zh: 我开始调查所有这些数字究竟有多可靠，以及这些公司对其方法的透明度如何。

sentences.en: Here's my story from 2018.
sentences.zh: 以下是我在2018年撰写的故事。

sentences.en: Sigrid Johnson was Black.
sentences.zh: 西格丽德·约翰逊是个黑人。

sentences.en: A DNA test said she wasn't.
sentences.zh: 但一项DNA测试说她不是。

sentences.zh: 由珍妮弗·拉沃伊朗读。

sentences.zh: 第一章。

sentences.en: Three years ago, when Sigrid E.
sentences.zh: 三年前，当西格丽德·E·

sentences.en: Johnson was 62, she got a call from a researcher seeking volunteers for a study on DNA ancestry tests and ethnic identity.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊62岁时，她接到了一位研究人员的电话，对方正在寻找研究DNA祖源测试和族裔认同的志愿者。

sentences.en: Johnson agreed to help.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊同意帮忙。

sentences.en: After all, she and the researcher, Anita Fomen, had been pals for half a century, ever since they attended the
sentences.zh: 毕竟，她和研究人员安妮塔·福门已经做了半个世纪的朋友，自从她们在费城融合社区的

sentences.en: same elementary school in their integrated Philadelphia neighborhood, where they and other Black children were mostly protected from the racism beyond its borders.
sentences.zh: 同一所小学上学以来就一直是朋友，在那里，她们和其他黑人儿童在很大程度上受到了保护，免受界限之外种族主义的侵害。

sentences.en: Fomen, a professor of communication at Westchester University in Pennsylvania, asked Johnson to swab the inside of
sentences.zh: 福门是宾夕法尼亚州韦斯特切斯特大学的传播学教授，她请约翰逊用棉签擦拭

sentences.en: her cheek and share her thoughts about her ethnic and racial identity before and after the results came back.
sentences.zh: 口腔内侧，并分享她在结果出来前后的族裔和种族认同的想法。

sentences.en: Johnson's father, a chauffeur who later became a superintendent at a housing project in North
sentences.zh: 约翰逊的父亲是一名司机，后来成为北

sentences.en: Philadelphia, had a golden brown complexion.
sentences.zh: 费城一个经济适用房项目的总管，他有着金黄色的皮肤。

sentences.en: Her mother, who said her own father was a white Brit, and her mother was half African American and half Native American, was light-skinned.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲皮肤白皙，曾说自己的父亲是白人英国人，母亲是一半非裔美国人和一半美洲原住民。

sentences.en: People sometimes mistook Johnson's mother for white, and when she applied for seamstress jobs at department stores in the 1920s and 30s, she chose not to correct them.
sentences.zh: 人们有时会误以为约翰逊的母亲是白人，当她在20世纪20年代和30年代申请百货公司的女裁缝工作时，她选择不纠正他们。

sentences.en: Sigrid, who had light caramel skin, was their only child, and her parents, Martha and Frank Gilchrist, doted on her.
sentences.zh: 西格丽德有着浅焦糖色的皮肤，是他们的独生女，她的父母玛莎和弗兰克·吉尔克里斯特对她疼爱有加。

sentences.en: In grade school, she prayed each night for an older brother, someone who would be fun to play with and would look after her, as her friend's brothers did with their siblings.
sentences.zh: 在上小学时，她每天晚上都祈祷能有一个哥哥，一个可以一起开心玩耍、照顾她的人，就像她朋友的哥哥对待他们的兄弟姐妹那样。

sentences.en: When she wasn't busy with ballet and piano lessons, she caught lightning bugs and played dolls, hopscotch, and jump rope with nearby friends.
sentences.zh: 当她不忙于芭蕾和钢琴课时，她会和附近的伙伴们一起抓萤火虫、玩洋娃娃、跳房子和跳绳。

sentences.en: The neighborhood, West Mount Airy, was a tree-lined community, one of the first in the nation to integrate successfully.
sentences.zh: 这个社区名叫西芒特艾瑞，是一个绿树成荫的社区，也是全美最早成功实现种族融合的社区之一。

sentences.en: It was populated mostly by middle and upper-class people, including many
sentences.zh: 这里主要居住着中产阶级和上流阶级人士，包括许多

sentences.en: African American professional men who had fair-skinned wives and children whose complexions matched their mothers.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国专业男性，他们的妻子皮肤白皙，孩子们的肤色也与母亲相配。

sentences.en: Johnson doesn't remember her parents talking much about race, except when her father made it clear that he expected her to marry a black man.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊不记得父母经常谈论种族问题，除非她父亲明确表示希望她嫁给一个黑人。

sentences.en: But even without that explicit talk, she was immersed in the highs and lows of black life.
sentences.zh: 但即使没有这种明确的谈话，她也沉浸在黑人生活的起起落落之中。

sentences.en: Her cousin, a surgeon named William Gilchrist
sentences.zh: 她的表弟，一位名叫威廉·吉尔克里斯特·

sentences.en: Anderson, lived in Albany, Georgia, where he led a large coalition of activists in the early 1960s to desegregate public facilities.
sentences.zh: 安德森的外科医生，住在佐治亚州奥尔巴尼，在20世纪60年代初，他领导了一场由大量活动家组成的联盟，旨在废除公共设施的种族隔离。

sentences.en: A friend and classmate of Ralph Abernathy, Anderson persuaded the Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
sentences.zh: 作为拉尔夫·阿伯内西的朋友和同班同学，安德森说服马丁·路德·金牧师

sentences.en: to participate in the city's demonstrations, which Johnson remembers she and her parents sometimes joined.
sentences.zh: 参与该市的示威游行，约翰逊记得她和父母有时也会加入其中。

sentences.en: During the family's trips to visit her cousin in Georgia,
sentences.zh: 在全家去佐治亚州探望表弟的旅途中，

sentences.en: Johnson saw water fountains that said, whites only.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊看到了写着“仅限白人”的饮水机。

sentences.en: And she still remembers the night that a giant cross burned near her cousin's front yard, and how he swept her and everyone else out of the house and put them all up in a hotel.
sentences.zh: 她仍然记得表弟前院附近燃烧巨大十字架的那天晚上，以及他是如何将她和家里所有人扫地出门并把他们全部安顿在酒店里的。

sentences.en: As a young teenager, Johnson pestered her mother about what it was like to give birth to her, a query her mother always dodged.
sentences.zh: 作为一个小青少年的约翰逊经常缠着母亲，问生下她是什么感觉，这个问题她的母亲总是闪烁其词。

sentences.en: But when Johnson was 16, her mother broke down and said through tears that they adopted her when she was an infant.
sentences.zh: 但当约翰逊16岁时，她的母亲情绪崩溃，泪流满面地告诉她，她在婴儿时期就被收养了。

sentences.en: Her mother explained that Johnson's biological father was black, and that her biological mother was a white Italian woman who said she
sentences.zh: 她的母亲解释说，约翰逊的亲生父亲是黑人，亲生母亲是一位白人意大利女性，对方说

sentences.en: couldn't keep the baby, who by then was two or three months old.
sentences.zh: 她无法抚养这个当时已经两三个月大的婴儿。

sentences.en: The woman, who lived in South
sentences.zh: 这位住在南

sentences.en: Philadelphia, had explained that she already had several children, all of whom were blonde, and that her white husband didn't want another man's child raised in his home.
sentences.zh: 费城的女性曾解释说，她已经有了几个孩子，而且全都是金发，她的白人丈夫不想在家里抚养另一个男人的孩子。

sentences.en: Not least of all, one whose color so boldly announced that fact.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，这个孩子的肤色如此大胆地宣示了这一事实。

sentences.en: Johnson's mother said the woman came to see the baby for about a year, until she asked the woman to stop visiting because she didn't want Sigrid to find out she was adopted.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊的母亲说，那个女人来看过婴儿大约一年，直到她要求那个女人停止探望，因为她不想让西格丽德发现自己是被收养的。

sentences.en: Johnson teared up as she recounted the conversation with her mother that took place 49 years ago.
sentences.zh: 在回忆49年前与母亲的那次谈话时，约翰逊热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: The news, all of it, was crushing, Johnson told me.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊对我说，所有的消息都是毁灭性的打击。

sentences.en: To this day, I honestly wish she had never told me.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我真的希望她从来没有告诉我。

sentences.en: I wanted my mom to be my mom.
sentences.zh: 我希望我的妈妈就是我的妈妈。

sentences.en: Neither one ever broached the subject with the other again.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，两人再也没有向对方提起过这个话题。

sentences.en: So when Anita Fomen requested that she take a DNA test, Johnson figured it was no big deal.
sentences.zh: 因此，当安妮塔·福门要求她做DNA测试时，约翰逊觉得这没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: She was half African and half Italian.
sentences.zh: 她有一半非洲血统和一半意大利血统。

sentences.en: I knew what the results would show when they came back, that is, until the results actually came back.
sentences.zh: 我知道结果出来后会显示什么，直到结果真正出来之前都是如此。

sentences.en: Two.
sentences.zh: 第二章。

sentences.en: Johnson is one of many millions of people around the world who have placed a bit of saliva
sentences.zh: 约翰逊是全球数百万将一小口唾液

sentences.en: into a DNA kit, sent it off to a testing company, waited a good month for the results, and then discovered the sometimes life-altering secrets hidden in those tiny drops.
sentences.zh: 放入DNA测试盒、寄给测试公司、满怀期待地等待整整一个月的结果、然后发现隐藏在那些微小水滴中有时会改变人生命运的秘密的人之一。

sentences.en: Virtually every cell in a human's body carries that person's whole unique blueprint, the double helix of DNA.
sentences.zh: 人体内的几乎每个细胞都携带者该人独特而完整的蓝图——DNA双螺旋结构。

sentences.en: The genes on chromosomes influence the traits of every living thing.
sentences.zh: 染色体上的基因影响着每个生物的特征。

sentences.en: Testing companies analyze hundreds of thousands of particular genetic sequences and use those snippets as clues to all sorts of information.
sentences.zh: 测试公司分析数十万个特定的基因序列，并将这些片段用作获取各种信息的线索。

sentences.en: Scientists have determined specific locations in the DNA code that provide hints about where your
sentences.zh: 科学家们已经确定了DNA密码中的特定位置，这些位置提供了关于你

sentences.en: ancestors came from, because people from the same geographical place share certain genetic similarities.
sentences.zh: 祖先来自哪里的线索，因为来自同一地理地方的人具有某些共同的遗传相似性。

sentences.en: The tests can also reveal your biological relatives and how closely you're related by evaluating how much of your and their DNA patterns overlap.
sentences.zh: 这些测试还可以通过评估你和他们的DNA模式重叠了多少，来揭示你的生物学亲属以及你们的血缘关系有多近。

sentences.en: In addition, DNA analysis can identify some of the hereditary disorders you may be predisposed to or may pass on to your children.
sentences.zh: 此外，DNA分析还可以识别你可能易患或可能遗传给孩子的某些遗传性疾病。

sentences.en: Rudimentary DNA testing has been around since the mid-20th century, but at-home genetic tests,
sentences.zh: 基本的DNA测试自20世纪中叶以来就已存在，但家用基因测试——

sentences.en: aside from simple paternity tests, didn't show up until this century, after the Human Genome
sentences.zh: 除了简单的亲子鉴定之外——直到本世纪才出现，当时人类基因组

sentences.en: Project prompted biotechnological advances that made genetic sequencing much more affordable.
sentences.zh: 项目推动了生物技术的进步，使基因测序变得更加实惠。

sentences.en: Most of those early personal genomic tests focused on genealogy, a way to fill out the family tree,
sentences.zh: 早期的大多数个人基因组测试都集中在谱系学上，作为一种完善族谱的方法，

sentences.en: because determining familial connections is scientifically much more straightforward than determining a person's true ethnic lineage.
sentences.zh: 因为在科学上，确定家族联系比确定一个人真正的族裔血统要直接得多。

sentences.en: But in 2007, as scientists linked more genes to diseases and traits, 23andMe pioneered a much broader kind of retail genomics, a $999 saliva test
sentences.zh: 但在2007年，随着科学家将更多的基因与疾病和特征联系起来，23andMe开创了一种更广泛的零售基因组学，这是一种售价999美元的唾液测试，

sentences.en: that promised to reveal genetic information from the novel to the profound.
sentences.zh: 承诺揭示从新奇到深奥的遗传信息。

sentences.en: It included ancestry and information about medical and other genetic information, including consumers' risk for age-related
sentences.zh: 它包括祖源信息以及医疗和其他遗传信息，包括消费者患年龄相关

sentences.en: macular degeneration, Parkinson's disease, and type 2 diabetes, as well as genes that block the bitter taste in vegetables and influence weight gain.
sentences.zh: 性黄斑变性、帕金森病和2型糖尿病的风险，以及阻断蔬菜中苦味和影响体重增加的基因。

sentences.en: The following year, Time magazine named the company's
sentences.zh: 第二年，《时代》杂志将该公司的

sentences.en: Retail DNA test, The Invention of the Year, describing this moment as the beginning of a personal genomics
sentences.zh: 零售DNA测试评为“年度发明”，并将这一时刻描述为个人基因组学

sentences.en: revolution that will transform not only how we take care of ourselves, but also what we mean by personal information.
sentences.zh: 革命的开始，这场革命不仅将改变我们照顾自己的方式，还将改变我们对个人信息的定义。

sentences.en: Not everything about how this information will be used is clear yet.
sentences.zh: 关于这些信息将如何被使用，并非所有事情现在都还清晰。

sentences.en: 23andMe has stirred up debate about issues ranging from how meaningful the results are,
sentences.zh: 23andMe引发了从结果有多大意义

sentences.en: to how to prevent genetic discrimination, but the curtain has been pulled back, and it can never be closed again.
sentences.zh: 到如何防止基因歧视等各种问题的争论，但帷幕已经拉开，就再也无法合上了。

sentences.en: Those debates continue, but in the last year or so, sales of at-home genetic tests have risen meteorically.
sentences.zh: 这些争论仍在继续，但在过去一年左右的时间里，家用基因测试的销量呈火箭式增长。

sentences.en: By April 2017, 23andMe had roughly 2 million customers, and this past January, just 9 months later, it had more than 5 million.
sentences.zh: 截至2017年4月，23andMe大约有200万客户，而在过去的1月，仅仅9个月后，客户就超过了500万。

sentences.en: AncestryDNA's customer base doubled to about 6 million in
sentences.zh: 仅在2017年一年，AncestryDNA的客户群就翻了一番，达到约600万，

sentences.en: 2017 alone, and has since grown to more than 10 million.
sentences.zh: 此后更是增长到了1000多万。

sentences.en: Add to that all the customers of MyHeritage,
sentences.zh: 再加上MyHeritage、

sentences.en: FamilyTreeDNA, Helix, National Geographic's DNA test, and dozens of others.

sentences.en: The most popular tests are those that promise to reveal test takers' ancestry and identify their relatives, and have the potential to upend our understanding of ourselves.

sentences.zh: 当到了选择大学的时候，她选择了一所500多英里以外的学校，那是俄亥俄州一所历史悠久的黑人大学，名叫威尔伯福斯，是以一位杰出的

sentences.en: At first, she felt self-conscious that she lacked the richly colored skin that was finally

sentences.en: While Johnson was at Wilberforce, she told no one that she was adopted, and no one that she was half-white.

sentences.zh: 在她周围，同班同学穿着非洲短衫和其他非洲服饰，或者戴着黑豹党的黑色贝雷帽和黑色皮夹克。

sentences.zh: 她的父母对这个男人皮肤的黑皙程度表示不满，因为根据他们的经验，较浅的肤色意味着更高的地位和更多的选择。

sentences.en: In 1985, she married another man, a physical therapiSt. By then, both her parents had died.
sentences.zh: 她把从未对除了儿子和几个至交好友之外的任何人说过的事告诉了她的丈夫。

sentences.en: She told her husband what she had never told anyone else besides her son and a few close friends.

sentences.en: Years later, he happened upon a conversation on the Phil Donahue show about adoptees successfully requesting their original birth certificates from state officials.
sentences.zh: 这正是促使她采取行动的契机。

sentences.zh: 她立刻在工作时给约翰逊打电话，鼓励她也去申请出生证明。

sentences.en: He gathered all the information she needed, and they sent it off together.
sentences.zh: 他收集了她需要的所有信息，然后他们一起把申请寄了出去。

sentences.en: When it arrived, she learned that her mother's name was Ann D'Amico.
sentences.zh: 证明寄到时，她得知自己母亲的名字叫安·达米科。

sentences.en: So Johnson and her husband called D'Amico's they found in the Philadelphia phone book.
sentences.zh: 于是，约翰逊和丈夫拨打了他们在费城电话簿上找到的达米科的电话。

sentences.zh: 达米科。

sentences.en: Others just hung up.
sentences.zh: 其他人直接挂断了电话。

sentences.en: Still, when Johnson took the DNA test in 2015 at age 62, she was certain about what it would find, and was sorry she wouldn't be able to share the results with her husband,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，2015年约翰逊在62岁时做DNA测试时，她对测试结果深信不疑，并遗憾自己无法与丈夫分享结果，

sentences.en: who had died years earlier.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫几年前已经去世了。

sentences.en: The results, which indicated a stunning level of precision, shocked Johnson.
sentences.zh: 这些显示出惊人精确度的结果让约翰逊大吃一惊。

sentences.zh: 我心想，那我到底是谁？

sentences.zh: 我知道以我的年纪，实在不该在意别人的看法，但我不好意思把结果给儿子和表妹以外的任何人看，她对我来说就像亲姐姐一样？

sentences.en: I was afraid people would think I was a fraud.
sentences.zh: 我害怕别人会觉得我是个骗子。

sentences.en: I was so disappointed, and in my heart of hearts, I didn't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我太失望了，内心深处我根本不相信这个结果。

sentences.en: Because how could I not be black?

sentences.en: With the stupendous rise of DNA ancestry testing, academics have wondered how those genetic results affect people's core identity.
sentences.zh: 随着DNA祖源测试的急剧兴起，学者们开始思考这些基因结果如何影响人们的核心身份认同。

sentences.en: Our sense of self, of course, is built on much more than just the ethnic tribe we belong to.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们的自我意识建立在远超我们所属族群的基础之上。

sentences.en: We forge our identity from the social and cultural milieus we're raised in, the messages we get from parents, teachers, and society about ourselves, the family lore and
sentences.zh: 我们的身份认同是由我们成长的社会与文化环境、父母、老师和社会的评价、代代相传的家族传说和

sentences.en: traditions passed down from generation to generation, and the experiences we have and hold dear.
sentences.zh: 传统，以及我们经历并珍视的体验共同塑造的。

sentences.en: All of that is deeply woven into who we are.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都深深交织在我们是谁的本质中。

sentences.en: Our identity is what grounds us and gives our lives meaning, said David Brzezinski, emeritus professor
sentences.zh: 罗格斯大学发育与临床心理学荣休教授大卫·布热津斯基表示，身份认同是我们的立足之本，赋予了我们的生活意义，他的研究重点是身份认同与收养。

sentences.en: of developmental and clinical psychology at Rutgers University, whose work focuses on identity and adoption.
sentences.zh: 罗格斯大学发育与临床心理学荣休教授大卫·布热津斯基表示，身份认同是我们的立足之本，赋予了我们的生活意义，他的研究重点是身份认同与收养。

sentences.en: That identity can be a motivating force or a debilitating one, depending on how we define ourselves and internalize the feedback we get from others.
sentences.zh: 这种身份认同可以成为一种动力，也可能是一种负担，这取决于我们如何定义自己以及如何内化他人给我们的反馈。

sentences.en: We spend our lives searching for self, though we each do that in different ways and at different times.
sentences.zh: 我们花了一生时间寻找自我，尽管我们每个人在不同时期、以不同的方式在做这件事。

sentences.en: It's all about the desire to fill in empty spaces, to find connection, to know more about yourself.
sentences.zh: 这一切都源于填补空白、寻找联系、更多地了解自己的渴望。

sentences.en: For children cut off from their origins because of a closed adoption or an unknown sperm or egg donor, those answers are harder to get.
sentences.zh: 对于因封闭式收养或未知的精子或卵子捐赠而与血统源头隔绝的孩子来说，这些答案更加难以获得。

sentences.en: And if a person's origin was a secret that they discover later in life, Brzezinski said, they may feel that everything they knew about themselves and their roots was a lie.
sentences.zh: 布热津斯基说，如果一个人的身世是一个秘密，而且他们在晚年才发现这个秘密，他们可能会觉得他们对自己和根源的一切认知都是谎言。

sentences.en: Even people who were raised by their biological parents can feel shaken when their DNA tests present results that don't fit with their understanding of who they are.
sentences.zh: 即使是由亲生父母抚养长大的人，当他们的DNA测试结果与他们对自我的认知不符时，也会感到动摇。

sentences.en: Anita Fomen is one of the academics studying the effects of unexpected DNA results.
sentences.zh: 安妮塔·福曼是研究意外DNA结果影响的学者之一。

sentences.en: Since 2006, she has tested roughly 3,000 people.
sentences.zh: 自2006年以来，她已经对大约3000人进行了测试。

sentences.en: Before her subjects receive their results, she asks them about their racial and ethnic identities, then follows up with them once the results are in.
sentences.zh: 在受试者获得结果之前，她会询问他们的种族和族裔身份，并在结果出来后进行跟进。

sentences.en: Her research subjects often conflate race and ethnicity.
sentences.zh: 她的研究对象经常混淆种族和族裔。

sentences.en: If I'm this color, my ancestors must be from this place.
sentences.zh: 如果我是这种肤色，我的祖先一定来自这个地方。

sentences.en: But ancestry tests, look for genetic links to geographic regions, not to physical characteristics associated with race,
sentences.zh: 但祖先测试寻找的是与地理区域的基因联系，而不是与种族相关的身体特征的联系，

sentences.en: like skin color, which is an unreliable indicator of ancestry.
sentences.zh: 比如肤色，它是一个不可靠的祖源指标。

sentences.en: Fomen and researchers at other universities have found that people accept the results that suit their aspirations,
sentences.zh: 福曼和其他大学的研究人员发现，人们往往会接受符合他们期望的结果，

sentences.en: and often dismiss results that challenge their long-held core beliefs.
sentences.zh: 而常常拒绝那些挑战他们长期持有的核心信念的结果。

sentences.en: We seek out and cultivate identities to fill our need to belong.
sentences.zh: 我们寻求并培养身份认同，以满足我们对归属感的需求。

sentences.en: And it's through that lens of identity that we see and understand the world, said J.
sentences.zh: 纽约大学心理学教授J.

sentences.en: Van Bavel, a psychology professor at New York
sentences.zh: 范巴韦尔研究群体身份、价值观和信念如何塑造思维和大脑，他表示，

sentences.en: University who researches how group identities, values, and beliefs shape the mind and brain.

sentences.en: So when you get information that challenges your identity, many people tune it out, just like we do with
sentences.zh: 因此，当你获得挑战你身份的信息时，许多人会选择忽视，就像我们对待

sentences.zh: 与我们的政治和信仰体系相悖的头条新闻和新闻报道一样。

sentences.en: When white test takers see results that indicate they have African ancestry, some, especially young people, welcome their newfound
sentences.zh: 当白人受试者看到显示他们有非洲血统的结果时，有些人，尤其是年轻人，会欢迎他们新发现的

sentences.en: multicultural heritage, even when the percentage is small, which raises an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 多元文化遗产，即使这个比例很小，这也引发了一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: For example, many blacks and whites whose families have long claimed that some of their forebears were

sentences.en: And Asians, like whites, often rebuff results that indicate that their heritage isn't pure.
sentences.zh: 亚裔和白人一样，经常拒绝表明其血统不纯的结果。

sentences.en: Some people take that to extremes.
sentences.zh: 有些人将这一点推向了极端。

sentences.zh: 利用DNA测试来证明其种族纯洁性的白人至上主义者坚决拒绝任何非欧洲血统的结果。

sentences.en: A professor at the University of California at Los Angeles and another researcher studied comments on the online white supremacist forum Stormfront.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚大学洛杉矶分校的一位教授和另一名研究人员研究了在线白人至上主义论坛Stormfront上的评论。

sentences.en: They found that some posters who had taken DNA tests and were upset with their results argued that they were rigged to spread multiculturalism, or that the
sentences.zh: 他们发现，一些做了DNA测试且对结果不满意的发帖者辩称，测试是被操纵以传播多元文化的，或者

sentences.en: non-European findings were merely noise DNA.
sentences.zh: 非欧洲血统的发现只是一种噪音DNA。

sentences.en: Many African Americans, meanwhile, upon seeing how much of their lineage is European, their lineage is European, are not necessarily surprised or doubtful about the results.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，许多非洲美国人在看到自己的血统中有很大一部分是欧洲血统时，他们的血统是欧洲血统，他们并不一定对结果感到惊讶或怀疑。

sentences.en: But they feel gut-punched by the bald reminder that even their genes carry slavery's legacy.

sentences.zh: 所有这些反应背后的核心问题都是身份认同。

sentences.en: Much of the jump in DNA test sales this past year or two has been a result of deeply discounted prices.
sentences.zh: 过去一两年里，DNA检测销量的大幅增长很大程度上归功于大幅折扣价。

sentences.en: They now cost about $99 and aggressive marketing as companies try to lure ever more people to give up their personal genetic code.
sentences.zh: 它们现在的价格约为99美元，各大公司通过激进的营销手段，试图诱使越来越多的人交出自己的个人密码。

sentences.en: Last year on Black Friday, 23andMe's discounted test was one of Amazon's five best-sellers.
sentences.zh: 去年的黑色星期五，23andMe的折扣检测成为了亚马逊五大畅销商品之一。

sentences.en: That same weekend, AncestryDNA reportedly sold a whopping 1.5 million kits.
sentences.zh: 据报道，就在那个周末，AncestryDNA售出了惊人的150万套检测盒。

sentences.en: In 2017, in a consumer guide to DNA Ancestry testing, the Council for Responsible Genetics wrote,
sentences.zh: 2017年，负责任基因委员会在发布的一份DNA祖源检测消费者指南中写道：

sentences.en: these come-ons promise more than they can deliver, ignoring problems with accuracy while obscuring a
sentences.zh: 这些诱饵许诺的远超它们所能兑现的，它们忽视了准确性方面的问题，同时掩盖了一种

sentences.en: business model in which customers pay for the privilege of giving away valuable information to venture capitalists who expect it will make them very, very rich.
sentences.zh: 商业模式：消费者付钱是为了获取将宝贵信息拱手让给风险投资机构的“特权”，而这些风投期望借此赚得盆满钵满。

sentences.en: Six.
sentences.zh: 第六部分。

sentences.en: In the last few years, just a few miles away from Sigrid Johnson, another woman's origin story was unfolding.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，就在离西格丽德·强森仅几英里远的地方，另一个女性的身世之谜正在徐徐揭开。

sentences.en: Her name is June Smith.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫琼·史密斯。

sentences.en: Like Johnson, Smith had no idea as a child that the parents who were raising her weren't the ones who created her.
sentences.zh: 和强森一样，史密斯在童年时根本不知道抚养她长大的父母并非她的亲生父母。

sentences.en: Smith's neighbors knew that the six-day-old baby who had suddenly appeared in the Smith house wasn't born to the Smiths, and they also understood that
sentences.zh: 史密斯的邻居们知道那个突然出现在史密斯家、出生仅六天的婴儿并不是史密斯夫妇亲生的，他们同时也明白，

sentences.en: fact was meant to remain private.
sentences.zh: 这个事实应当被严格保密。

sentences.en: So for years, neighbors knew more about Smith's origins than she herself did.
sentences.zh: 因此多年来，邻居们对史密斯身世的了解比她本人还要多。

sentences.en: In their solidly black neighborhood in South Philadelphia, Smith stood out.
sentences.zh: 在南费城那个清一色黑人居住的社区里，史密斯显得格外显眼。

sentences.en: Her skin was lighter than most, and her hair was wavy and long, like a white girl's, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，她的肤色比大多数人浅，头发又长又卷，就像一个白人女孩。

sentences.en: Though she had some good friends, she was bullied by others.
sentences.zh: 尽管她有一些好朋友，但她也遭到过其他人的霸凌。

sentences.en: Automatically, I was a target because darker people thought that a lighter-colored person is more privileged, Smith told me.
sentences.zh: 史密斯告诉我：“我自然而然地成了靶子，因为肤色较深的人认为肤色较浅的人享有更多特权。”

sentences.en: I wasn't black enough.
sentences.zh: 我黑得不够彻底。

sentences.en: Like Johnson, Smith learned startling news about herself when she was 16, when a neighborhood friend let slip that Smith's parents weren't her real parents.
sentences.zh: 和强森一样，史密斯在16岁时得知了关于自己的惊人消息，当时一个社区朋友说漏了嘴，透露史密斯的父母并非她的亲生父母。

sentences.en: Smith marched inside to interrogate her mother, who chided her for asking such crazy questions.
sentences.zh: 史密斯气冲冲地走进屋里质问母亲，母亲却责备她怎么问出这种荒唐的问题。

sentences.en: Eventually, her parents confessed.
sentences.zh: 最终，她的父母向她坦白了。

sentences.en: They described a white Italian woman who handed over her six-day-old infant, after explaining that the father was black and adding, I can't take that baby home.
sentences.zh: 他们描述了一个白人意大利妇女，她交出了出生仅六天的婴儿，并解释说孩子的父亲是个黑人，还补充道：“我不能把这个孩子带回家。”

sentences.en: If I do, they'll kill her.
sentences.zh: “如果我这么做了，他们会杀了她的。”

sentences.en: Smith told me, I never knew if my mom added that last part, but I know she never wanted me to know that woman, so she may have said it to deter me.
sentences.zh: 史密斯告诉我：“我从来不知道我妈妈是不是自己加上了最后那部分，但我知道她绝不想让我找到那个女人，所以她可能为了阻止我才这么说的。”

sentences.en: Then again, it was part of that era.
sentences.zh: 话又说回来，这也是那个时代的写照。

sentences.en: Either way, I grew up with a lot of animosity toward that white woman.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我在对那个白人女人的满腔怨恨中长大。

sentences.en: The idea that she didn't want me just was black.
sentences.zh: 她不想要我的这种想法简直糟透了。

sentences.en: Smith's mother showed June her original birth certificate.
sentences.zh: 史密斯的母亲向琼展示了她最初的出生证明。

sentences.en: It said she was
sentences.zh: 上面写着她是

sentences.en: Gail Moser.
sentences.zh: 盖尔·莫瑟。

sentences.en: The news shook Smith's understanding of who she was.
sentences.zh: 这个消息动摇了史密斯对自身身份的认知。

sentences.en: The search for identity that's so central to adolescence took on extra urgency.
sentences.zh: 对青少年时期至关重要的身份认同寻找变得更加紧迫。

sentences.en: For starters, she said, I couldn't imagine a white woman gave birth to me.
sentences.zh: 她说：“首先，我无法想象一个白人妇女竟然生下了我。”

sentences.en: So Smith did what she could to reconcile the two versions of her life.
sentences.zh: 于是，史密斯尽其所能去调和她人生的两个版本。

sentences.en: Her high school was predominantly white and disproportionately Italian-American, so I began hanging out with white kids and started acting and dressing like a punk rocker,
sentences.zh: 她的高中白人学生居多，且意大利裔比例过高，所以“我开始和白人群体混在一起，开始像朋克摇滚乐手一样行事和着装”，

sentences.en: because I thought that's what white kids did.
sentences.zh: 因为我以为那是白人小孩会做的事。

sentences.en: I went through a total change.
sentences.zh: 我经历了一场脱胎换骨的巨变。

sentences.en: I told the white kids I was half Italian.
sentences.zh: 我告诉白人小孩我是意大利混血。

sentences.en: I actually felt they were more accepting of me than my black peers were.
sentences.zh: 我实际上觉得他们比我的黑人同龄人更能接纳我。

sentences.en: Smith never denied she was black, but she didn't embrace it either once she found out she was half white.
sentences.zh: 史密斯从未否认自己是黑人，但自从发现自己有一半白人血统后，她也没有全然接受自己的黑人身份。

sentences.en: It wasn't until she was in her 30s, as her self-esteem solidified, that she welcomed back her black identity.
sentences.zh: 直到她三十多岁、自我价值感逐渐巩固时，她才重新接纳了自己的黑人身份。

sentences.en: I saw how society treated people of color, and I thought, you know, black people raised me.
sentences.zh: “我看到了社会是如何对待有色人种的，我想，你知道的，是黑人把我养大的。”

sentences.en: And so I became more conscious that, culturally, that's who I am.
sentences.zh: “因此我变得更加清醒地意识到，从文化上讲，这就是我。”

sentences.en: Had her birth mother raised her, she said, I'd probably consider myself white, because I would have grown up in that Italian home.
sentences.zh: 她说，如果她的亲生母亲抚养了她，“我可能会认为自己是白人，因为我会在那个意大利家庭里长大。”

sentences.en: I would have grown up with Italian ways, Italian foods, Italian whatever.
sentences.zh: “我会在意大利的生活方式、意大利食物以及各种意大利习俗中长大。”

sentences.en: But because of how I was raised, African-American, this is who I am, and I accept that, and I'm proud of it.
sentences.zh: 但由于我的成长环境是非洲裔美国人，这就是现在的我，我接受这一点，并且为此感到骄傲。

sentences.en: Although her cultural identity was clear by then, she still yearned to know about her biological family.
sentences.zh: 尽管到那时她的文化认同已经很清晰了，但她仍然渴望了解自己的亲生家庭。

sentences.en: She wrote and self-published her autobiography in 2014.
sentences.zh: 她在2014年写作并自费出版了自己的自传。

sentences.en: The last line says,
sentences.zh: 最后一行的内容是：

sentences.en: I am the product of someone, but the reflection of no one.
sentences.zh: 我是某人的产物，却不是任何人的倒影。

sentences.en: Seven.
sentences.zh: 第七部分。

sentences.en: AncestryDNA and 23andMe give their users the option to have their DNA profile uploaded to see if any genetic relatives pop up.
sentences.zh: AncestryDNA和23andMe为用户提供了一个选项，即将他们的DNA档案上传，以查看是否有任何基因亲戚出现。

sentences.en: Johnson did so, curious, but expecting little.
sentences.zh: 强森这样做了，她既好奇，又没抱太大希望。

sentences.en: AncestryDNA promptly revealed two women whose DNA indicated that they were close family, which Johnson thought meant they were her first cousins.
sentences.zh: AncestryDNA很快显示出两名女性，她们的DNA表明她们是近亲，强森认为这意味着她们是她的表亲。

sentences.en: She reached out to them.
sentences.zh: 她联系了她们。

sentences.en: One never responded.
sentences.zh: 其中一人从未回复。

sentences.en: The other was June Smith.
sentences.zh: 另一个人是琼·史密斯。

sentences.en: In late August, Johnson and Smith connected by phone.
sentences.zh: 八月下旬，强森和史密斯通过电话取得了联系。

sentences.en: After introducing themselves, Smith asked Johnson if she was adopted.
sentences.zh: 在互相做完自我介绍后，史密斯问强森是否被收养过。

sentences.en: Johnson said yes.
sentences.zh: 强森说是的。

sentences.en: Smith asked, was your biological mother Anne D'Amico?
sentences.zh: 史密斯问：“你的亲生母亲是安妮·达米科吗？”

sentences.en: Johnson was startled that this stranger would know such a thing.
sentences.zh: 强森大吃一惊，一个陌生人竟然会知道这种事。

sentences.en: Smith then asked what her birth name was.
sentences.zh: 接着，史密斯问她出生时的名字是什么。

sentences.en: When Johnson said, Joan Moser,
sentences.zh: 当强森说出“琼·莫瑟”时，

sentences.en: Smith started to cry.
sentences.zh: 史密斯哭了起来。

sentences.en: She said, I've been looking for Joan Moser.
sentences.zh: 她说：“我一直在找琼·莫瑟。”

sentences.en: For you.
sentences.zh: “在找你。”

sentences.en: All these years.
sentences.zh: 这些年一直都在找。

sentences.en: Each knew she wasn't really a child of Eric Moser, D'Amico's white husband, despite his name being on their birth certificates.
sentences.zh: 尽管她们出生证明上写着埃里克·莫瑟（达米科的白人丈夫）的名字，但两人都知道自己并不是他的亲生骨肉。

sentences.en: These babies had black fathers, presumably two different men, given that Johnson and Smith's DNA results indicate that they are half-siblings, not full ones.
sentences.zh: 这些婴儿都有黑人父亲，鉴于强森和史密斯的DNA结果显示她们是同母异父而非全亲生姐妹，这两个父亲大概率是不同的人。

sentences.en: Smith told Johnson that she discovered her first Moser connection in 2015, a half-sister named Nancy Moser,
sentences.zh: 史密斯告诉强森，她在2015年发现了自己与莫瑟家族的第一个联系，那是一个名叫南希·莫瑟的同父异母（或同母异父）姐姐，

sentences.en: who told her that D'Amico had six white children, all of whom D'Amico raised.
sentences.zh: 南希告诉她，达米科有六个白人孩子，全都是由达米科抚养长大的。

sentences.en: Moser said that their parents had died, and that on D'Amico's deathbed, their mother conceded that she had other children, and added, I wonder if they made it.
sentences.zh: 莫瑟说他们的父母已经去世，在达米科临终之际，他们的母亲承认自己还有其他孩子，并补充道：“不知道他们有没有活下来。”

sentences.en: Smith had been swiftly enfolded into the Moser family, a comforting but also confusing experience.
sentences.zh: 史密斯很快融入了莫瑟家族，这是一次令人宽慰却又感到困惑的经历。

sentences.en: The siblings had told her she wasn't the only biracial child.
sentences.zh: 兄弟姐妹们告诉她，她并不是唯一的混血儿。

sentences.en: They told her that three years before Smith's birth, when at least some of D'Amico's children were already in grade school, D'Amico gave birth to a baby she named Joan.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉她，在史密斯出生前三年，当时达米科的一些孩子已经上了小学，达米科生下了一个婴儿，并给她取名为琼。

sentences.en: After two or three months, according to Moser lore, someone told D'Amico's white husband that Joan, whose skin was darker than her siblings, couldn't be his child.
sentences.zh: 根据莫瑟家族的传说，两三个月后，有人告诉达米科的白人丈夫，琼的肤色比她的兄弟姐妹更深，不可能是他的孩子。

sentences.en: She was black, so she had to go.
sentences.zh: 她是黑人，所以必须离开。

sentences.en: Smith described how welcoming the Moser siblings had been, and how the eldest told her she thought Smith might have a twin
sentences.zh: 史密斯描述了莫瑟家族的兄弟姐妹们是多么热情，老大还告诉她，她觉得史密斯可能还有一个双胞胎

sentences.en: sister, though she has never shown up on Smith's AncestryDNA page.
sentences.zh: 姐姐，尽管她从未在史密斯的AncestryDNA页面上出现过。

sentences.en: But a few years back, AncestryDNA linked Smith to a niece whose deceased father, Thomas, was another biracial child of Anne D'Amico.
sentences.zh: 但几年前，AncestryDNA将史密斯与一个侄女联系在了一起，该侄女已故的父亲托马斯也是安妮·莫瑟的另一个混血孩子。

sentences.en: The Mosers welcomed his family, too.
sentences.zh: 莫瑟家族也同样热情地接纳了他的家人。

sentences.en: After Smith and Johnson talked, Smith alerted the Moser siblings that Joan Moser was alive and well.
sentences.zh: 在史密斯和强森交谈之后，史密斯通知莫瑟家族的兄弟姐妹们，琼·莫瑟还活着并且过得很好。

sentences.en: Johnson was flooded with warm texts, phone calls, and Facebook messages from the Moser family.
sentences.zh: 强森收到了来自莫瑟家族大量充满暖意的短信、电话和脸书消息。

sentences.en: All at once, Johnson said, I got, I'm your brother, I'm your sister,
sentences.zh: 强森说，刹那间，“我收到了‘我是你兄弟’、‘我是你姐姐’、

sentences.en: I'm your cousin, I'm your sister's daughter.
sentences.zh: ‘我是你表亲’、‘我是你姐姐的女儿’这样的信息。”

sentences.en: Though they were total strangers, they embraced her as they had Smith, writing, Hi, honey, I'm one of your sisters.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们是完全的陌生人，但他们像接纳史密斯一样接纳了她，写道：“嗨，亲爱的，我是你的姐妹之一。”

sentences.en: Love you.
sentences.zh: “爱你的。”

sentences.en: I'm glad to know you're in our family now.
sentences.zh: “很高兴知道你现在加入了我们的大家庭。”

sentences.en: And I accept you no matter what color you are, and I can't wait to meet you.
sentences.zh: “无论你是什么肤色我都接受你，我迫不及待想见你。”

sentences.en: Just remember you are accepted into our family because you are family, and we love you.
sentences.zh: “只要记住你被我们的家庭接纳是因为我们是一家人，我们爱你。”

sentences.en: When Johnson saw a photo of Thomas, she was stunned by how much he looked like her son, Ron.
sentences.zh: 当强森看到托马斯的一张照片时，她被他与她儿子罗恩的相像程度惊呆了。

sentences.en: That family resemblance made the connection all the more real.
sentences.zh: 这种家族相似性让这份血缘联系变得更加真实。

sentences.en: It all hit me real hard, Johnson told me.
sentences.zh: 强森对我说：“这一切对我的冲击太真实了。”

sentences.en: I cried and boo-hooed like a baby.
sentences.zh: “我哭得像个婴儿一样嚎啕大哭。”

sentences.en: She went from being an only child to a woman with a slew of siblings, nieces, and nephews.
sentences.zh: 她从一个独生子女变成了一个拥有成群兄弟姐妹、侄子侄女的女性。

sentences.en: After two days packed with catching up on 65 years of family, Johnson stopped answering calls and reading texts.
sentences.zh: 在度过了整整两天、忙于补上落后65年的家庭生活之后，强森停止了接听电话和查看短信。

sentences.en: Overwhelmed, she went to church to calm her soul and express her gratitude.
sentences.zh: 由于情绪过度激动，她去了教堂来平复心情并表达感激之情。

sentences.en: And then she dove right back in with her new old clan.
sentences.zh: 随后，她又一头扎回了她这个新的“老”家族中。

sentences.en: Since then, she still sometimes feels dizzy as she tries to replace a long familiar identity with a welcome but much more complicated one.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，当她试图用一个受欢迎但复杂得多的身份去取代那个熟悉已久的身份时，有时仍然会感到一阵眩晕。

sentences.en: She marvels that for all those decades as a single child, she had siblings galore living only a few miles away, and she never knew it.
sentences.zh: 她感到惊奇的是，在作为独生子女度过的那些数十家里，她明明有成群的兄弟姐妹就住在仅仅几英里外，而她却一无所知。

sentences.en: One of them even looked like her, and had been told the same lie about her origins, and then the same gut-wrenching truth.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人甚至长得像她，被灌输了关于自己身世的同一个谎言，后来又得知了同样让人揪心的真相。

sentences.en: Smith so deeply understood Johnson's experience because she had lived it herself, as a sister would.
sentences.zh: 史密斯对强森的经历感同身受，因为她自己也经历过这一切，就像一个真正的姐姐那样。

sentences.en: A real sister.
sentences.zh: 一个亲姐姐。

sentences.en: Finally.
sentences.zh: 终于。

sentences.en: Those realities were far more mind-bending than any of the ancestry findings, with their wildly different percentages and ephemeral certainties.
sentences.zh: 这些现实远比任何祖源检测结果更令人颠覆认知，那些检测充斥着天差地别的百分比和转瞬即逝的确定性。

sentences.en: Johnson and Smith talked two or three times every day.
sentences.zh: 强森和史密斯每天通两到三次电话。

sentences.en: We're stuck on each other, Johnson said.
sentences.zh: 强森说：“我们黏上彼此了。”

sentences.en: She sighed.
sentences.zh: 她叹了口气。

sentences.en: You turn 65, take a DNA test, and find out your whole life is a lot different than you ever thought it was.
sentences.zh: “你到了65岁，做了一次DNA检测，然后发现你的一生与你曾经想象的有着天壤之别。”

sentences.en: This was recorded by Autumn.
sentences.zh: 这段内容由Autumn录制。

sentences.en: Autumn is an app you can download to listen to lots of audio stories from publishers such as the New
sentences.zh: Autumn是一款你可以下载的应用程序，用于收听来自各大出版机构的大量音频故事，这些机构包括《纽约

sentences.en: York Times, The New Yorker, Vanity Fair, and The Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 时报》、《纽约客》、《名利场》和《大西洋月刊》。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
